The capital of Australia is Canberra. It was chosen as a compromise between the two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne, which had been engaged in a rivalry for the national capital's location.

Following the Federation of Australia in 1901, there was significant debate over whether Sydney or Melbourne should serve as the seat of government. Sydney was the largest and most populous city, while Melbourne was the financial and cultural hub. Neither city was willing to cede its status to the other. To resolve the impasse, the Australian Constitution mandated that the seat of government be located within the Commonwealth, but not within the territory of any state. Heat pump
Thermodynamics
Coefficient of performance
Thermodynamic cycle

A heat pump moves more heat than the electricity it consumes by transferring existing thermal energy from one location to another rather than generating heat through electrical resistance. This process relies on the thermodynamic principle that heat naturally flows from warmer areas to cooler areas, and the pump uses work to reverse this flow, effectively "pumping" ambient heat into a space.

The efficiency is measured by the Coefficient of Performance (COP), which is the ratio of heat energy moved to the electrical energy used. Because the system moves three to four units of heat for every one unit of electricity consumed, the COP is typically between 3 and 4. This exceeds the theoretical limit of resistive heating, where one unit of electricity yields only one unit of heat.
